mappet.commands.mp.help: Main Mappet command that provides subcommands for working with Mappet's features.
mappet.commands.mp.state.help:
State management subcommand.

§7<target>§r argument is used to determine where to edit the state. You can either specify player's name to edit player's states or §7~§r for global state.
mappet.commands.mp.state.add: This command adds §7<value>§r to state by §7<id>§r key. If §7<id>§r state doesn't exist or was a string, §7<value>§r will be added to 0.
mappet.commands.mp.state.clear: This command removes state by §7[id]§r key. If §7[id]§r was omitted, then all values will be erased. You can use §7*§r as a wildcard in §7[id]§r to remove multiple keys.
mappet.commands.mp.state.if:
This command evaluates §7<expression>§r against value §7<id>§r state, and if resulted §7<expression>§r is a non-zero value it does nothing, but if if outputs zero then the command will error.

This is useful for command blocks that can stop on errors.
mappet.commands.mp.state.print: This command prints out all the values §7<target>§r state has.
mappet.commands.mp.state.set: This command assigns §7<value>§r (it can be a number or an arbitrary string) to §7<id>§r key.
mappet.commands.mp.state.sub: This command subtracts §7<value>§r from state by §7<id>§r. If §7<id>§r state didn't exist or was a string, §7<value>§r will be subtracted from 0.
mappet.commands.mp.quest.accept: This command gives a quest by §7<id>§r from quest database to one or multiple §7<player>§r(s). If §7<player>§r(s) has this quest, then it will be ignored.
mappet.commands.mp.quest.complete: This command completes the quest (regardless whether player has needed objectives completed) by §7<id>§r for one or multiple §7<player>§r(s).
mappet.commands.mp.quest.decline: This command removes the quest by §7<id>§r from one or multiple §7<player>§r(s).
mappet.commands.mp.crafting.open: This command opens a crafting table by §7<id>§r for §7<player>§r(s).
mappet.commands.mp.crafting.drop:
This command drops an output item stacks from a crafting table by §7<id>§r from its recipe at index §7[index]§r at §7[x] [y] [z]§r.

§7[x] [y] [z]§r support relative position using §7~§r and can be omitted. §7[index]§r can be also §7@r§r which means it will use a random recipe. §7[mx] [my] [mz]§r can be provided to setup initial velocity of item entities.
mappet.commands.mp.event.trigger: This command triggers an event by §7<id>§r using player(s) or server (if §7~§r was passed) found by §7<target>§r selector as a context. You can also pass arbitrary NBT data to the event using §7[data]§r argument.
mappet.commands.mp.event.stop: This command stops a delayed event(s) (or script(s)) by given §7<id>§r.
mappet.commands.mp.dialogue.open: This command opens a dialogue by §7<id>§r for §7<player>§r(s). You can also pass arbitrary NBT data to the event using §7[data]§r argument.
mappet.commands.mp.npc.edit: This command allows to change an individual §7<property>§r to given §7<value>§r of NPC(s) found by §7<target>§r selector.
mappet.commands.mp.npc.state:
This command allows to switch the §7<state>§r of NPC(s) found by §7<target>§r selector.

§7<state>§r argument supports following format: §7[npc_id@]state[:properties]§r, where §7npc_id§r and §7properties§r are optional.

With this format, you can change the state from another NPC blueprint, or even change only certain properties from another state.
mappet.commands.mp.npc.summon: This command spawns an NPC with §7<id>§r with optional §7[state]§r (§7default§r is the default name of the state) at §7[x] [y] [z]§r. If §7[x] [y] [z]§r are omitted, then NPC will be spawned at place of command sender. Relative §7~§r is supported.
mappet.commands.mp.npc.despawn: This command despawns all NPCs found by §7<target>§r.
mappet.commands.mp.faction.help: Faction management subcommand. This command allows to manage faction score of individual or multiple players.
mappet.commands.mp.faction.add: This command adds faction score evaluated by §7<expression>§r to faction by §7<id>§r. If §7<id>§r doesn't exist, §7<expression>§r will be added to 0.
mappet.commands.mp.faction.clear: This command removes faction score of a faction by §7[id]§r. If §7[id]§r was omitted, then all faction score will be erased.
mappet.commands.mp.faction.set: This command assigns faction score evaluated by §7<expression>§r to faction by §7<id>§r.
mappet.commands.mp.data.help: Data utility subcommand that provides an ability to manage player inventory and states, and global state.
mappet.commands.mp.data.clear: Clears all global and player states, and optionally all player inventories. If §7[inventory]§r is omitted, then player inventories won't be cleared.
mappet.commands.mp.data.load: Loads saved data by §7<id>§r. §7[global]§r determines whether global states should be loaded too (it's §7true§r (enabled) by default). §7[players]§r allows to pick another player whose inventory and player states should be loaded to.
mappet.commands.mp.data.save: Saves global states, and current player's states and inventory to data by §7<id>§r.
mappet.commands.mp.script.eval: This command executes JS code snippet provided in §7<code...>§r. Variable §7c§r is provided which is a §7IScriptEvent§r which has either player subject (if the command was executed from player) or with server.
mappet.commands.mp.script.exec: This command executes script by §7<id>§r (from world's §7mappet/scripts/§r folder, without file extension) upon player(s) or server (if §7~§r was provided) found by §7<target>§r selector. Script's §7[function]§r (§7main§r if omitted) function will be called. You can also pass arbitrary NBT data to the event using §7[data]§r argument.
mappet.commands.mp.script.engines: This command returns a list of found script engines.
mappet.commands.mp.hud.close: Closes an HUD scene by §7[id]§r of all players found by §7<target>§r selector. If player(s) didn't have such HUD scene by §7[id]§r nothing will happen. If §7[id]§r was omitted, then all HUD scenes will be removed from players by §7<target>§r selector.
mappet.commands.mp.hud.morph: Changes the morph in player's scene by §7<id>§r for all players matching §7<target>§r selector at given §7<index>§r in the scene with a morph constructed from §7<nbt>§r. If the player won't have the scene, or a HUD morph at given §7<index>§r, nothing will happen.
mappet.commands.mp.hud.setup: Adds an HUD scene by §7<id>§r which will display to all players found by §7<target>§r selector. If scene by given §7<id>§r was already added earlier, and didn't expire, then it will be started over again.
mappet.commands.mp.morph.add.help: Subcommand to display morph(s) in the world.
mappet.commands.mp.morph.add.entity: Displays a §7<morph>§r in the world for §7<expiration>§r ticks attached to all entities found by §7<target>§r selector. §7<x>§r, §7<y>§r and §7<z>§r is a relative shift from the bottom center of entity's hit box. §7<rotate>§r is a boolean (§7true§r or §7false§r) that toggles whether world morph should follow entity's rotation. §7<yaw>§r and §7<pitch>§r are horizontal and vertical rotation offsets, respectively.
mappet.commands.mp.morph.add.world: Displays a §7<morph>§r in the world for §7<expiration>§r ticks.§7<x>§r, §7<y>§r and §7<z>§r are absolute world coordinates where the morph will be displayed. §7<yaw>§r and §7<pitch>§r are horizontal and vertical rotation offsets, respectively. Relative §7~§r values are supported for §7<x>§r, §7<y>§r, §7<z>§r, §7<yaw>§r, and §7<pitch>§r arguments.

mappet.gui.scripted_item.descriptions.in: This trigger fires when the player interacts with air (empty space) while holding a scripted item. The variables provided in the context are §6x§r, §6y§r, §6z§r coordinates of the interaction, and §6hand§r the hand used for the interaction.
This trigger fires when the player interacts with an entity while holding a scripted item. The variables provided in the context are the §6hand§r the player used to interact with the entity.

This trigger fires when the player interacts with a block while holding a scripted item. The variables provided in the context are §6x§r, §6y§r, §6z§r coordinates of the block, §6block§r the block's registry name, §6meta§r the block's meta-data, and §6hand§r the hand used for the interaction.
mappet.gui.scripted_item.descriptions.at: This trigger fires when the player attacks an entity while holding a scripted item. The variable provided in the context is §6damage§r the amount of damage dealt to the entity.
mappet.gui.scripted_item.descriptions.br: This trigger fires when the player breaks a block while holding a scripted item. The variables provided in the context are §6x§r, §6y§r, §6z§r coordinates of the block, §6block§r the block's registry name, and §6meta§r the block's meta-data.
mappet.gui.scripted_item.descriptions.pl: This trigger fires when the player places a block while holding a scripted item. The variables provided in the context are §6x§r, §6y§r, §6z§r coordinates of the block, §6block§r the block's registry name, §6meta§r the block's meta-data, and §6hand§r the hand used for the action.
mappet.gui.scripted_item.descriptions.hi: This trigger fires when the player hits a block while holding a scripted item. The variables provided in the context are §6x§r, §6y§r, §6z§r coordinates of the block, and §6hand§r the hand used for the action.
mappet.gui.scripted_item.descriptions.on: This trigger fires on each game tick when the player is holding the scripted item. The variable provided in the context is §6hand§r the hand that's holding the item.
mappet.gui.scripted_item.descriptions.pi: This trigger fires when the player picks up a scripted item. The variable provided in the context is §6item§r the item stack that was picked up, and §6entityItem§r §7IScriptEntityItem§r entity item that player picked.
mappet.gui.scripted_item.descriptions.to: This trigger fires when the player toss a scripted item. The variable provided in the context is §6item§r the item stack that was tossed, and §6entityItem§r §7IScriptEntityItem§r entity item that player tossed.
mappet.gui.scripted_item.descriptions.fi: This trigger fires when the player picks up a scripted item for the first time. The variable provided in the context is §6item§r the item stack that was picked up, and §6entityItem§r §7IScriptEntityItem§r entity item that player picked.
mappet.gui.scripted_item.descriptions.st: This trigger fires when the player starts holding a scripted item. The variable provided in the context is §6item§r the item stack that was picked up.
This trigger fires when the player stops holding a scripted item. The variable provided in the context is §6item§r the item stack that was picked up.
mappet.gui.scripted_item.descriptions.us: This trigger fires when the player starts using the scripted item. The variables provided in the context are §item§r the item stack that has been started being used and §6duration§r the duration of the use.

This trigger fires when the player stops using the scripted item. The variables provided in the context are §item§r the item stack that has been stopped being used and §6duration§r the duration of the use.
mappet.gui.scripted_item.descriptions.on: This trigger fires at each tick while the player is using the scripted item. The variables provided are §item§r the item stack that is being used and §6duration§r the duration of the use.
mappet.gui.scripted_item.descriptions.fi: This trigger fires when the player finishes using the scripted item. The variables provided are §item§r the item stack that has been used and §6duration§r the duration of the use.

mappet.gui.scripts.repl.welcome:
This is Mappet's Read-Eval-Print Loop (REPL). You can type in §6JS§r code, and execute it by pressing Enter key. You can cycle through eval history by holding §6Ctrl§r key and arrow §6Up§r or §6Down§r.

Following variables are available:

- §6c§r is a IScriptEvent that has player as a subject
- §6s§r is a IScriptPlayer
- §6mappet§r is a IScriptFactory

You can execute §7clear()§r function to clear all messages on the screen.

mappet.gui.ui_editor.label: Text
mappet.gui.client_settings.title: Client triggers
mappet.gui.client_settings.triggers.desc:
This trigger gets triggered on the §6client§r when the player interacts with a block (by right clicking it).

Unlike the server-side trigger, this one runs entirely on the client and sends nothing to the server, which makes it suitable for local sounds, particles and animations.

§lImportant§r: it fires before the server validates the interaction, so it also fires when the click ends up being rejected.
mappet.gui.client_settings.triggers.vari:
§6block§r, the ID of the block that was interacted with (like §7minecraft:stone§r).
§6meta§r, the meta value of the block's state.
§6x§r, §6y§r, and §6z§r in the world.
§6hand§r, the hand that interacted with the block (§7main§r or §7off§r).
mappet.gui.client_settings.triggers.desc:
This trigger gets triggered on the §6client§r when the player starts breaking a block (by left clicking it).

Unlike the server-side trigger, this one runs entirely on the client and sends nothing to the server, which makes it suitable for local sounds, particles and animations.

§lImportant§r: in creative mode holding the left mouse button re-fires this trigger every few ticks.
mappet.gui.client_settings.triggers.vari:
§6block§r, the ID of the block that was clicked (like §7minecraft:stone§r).
§6meta§r, the meta value of the block's state.
§6x§r, §6y§r, and §6z§r in the world.
§6hand§r, always §7main§r.
mappet.gui.client_settings.triggers.desc:
This trigger gets triggered on the §6client§r every game tick while the player is in the world.

Unlike the server-side trigger, this one runs entirely on the client and sends nothing to the server, which makes it suitable for local sounds, particles and animations.
